reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) discusses general magnetocaloric requirements, rare-earth-free alloys, and magnetic properties of other high-entropy systems, but none provides specific prior data on FeMnNiGeSi alloys, rapid solidification effects, or the link between nanostructuring and hysteresis reduction. premises: Rapid solidification produces a nanostructured microstructure in FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Nanostructuring increases grain boundary density and nucleation sites.
Increased nucleation sites spread the magnetostructural transition over a wider temperature/field interval.
A spread-out transition reduces hysteresis losses during low-field magnetic cooling.
The magnetocaloric entropy change amplitude is not completely sacrificed by this broadening.
